account:
Today’s business has been mostly routine, but a vague rumour about a bridge or port change keeps circulating. The neighbour mentioned it at the mill, and townsfolk have repeated it; one recently linked it to the bakery. I have seen no evidence of an actual change. The builder reported passable west-bank roads and no confirmed hazard, repair work, or costs. The secretary says the baker denies announcing any crossing or delivery change and confirmed normal operations; the innkeeper likewise had only an unspecified rumour. I cannot tell where the story began or whether it serves any purpose beyond people passing along uncertain news.

At my ten o’clock mill inspection I found 128 hay bales in the sale chest and left them untouched. That establishes stock quantity, not grain quality or delivery needs. Neither the neighbour nor freight could identify a confirmed shortage or transport order. Freight said the warehouse had space and would ask the baker about definite needs before moving stock. That appears to be ordinary coordination, not evidence of a planned crossing change.

I returned for the thirteen o’clock council letters. The secretary has received no new correspondence and says the morning record is secured in the appointments chest. I reported the inspection and requested a record that no grain transport was authorized. No repair spending has been approved without itemized proposals. It is now shortly after fourteen; my next appointment is tea with the neighbour at the east-bank dockside cottage at fifteen, followed by office at sixteen-thirty. I should keep those appointments and distinguish direct reports from rumour.
